title: Sex hormone replacement: testosterone, oestrogen and progestin
ariaLabel: Schematic of sex steroid replacement: testosterone acts on androgen receptors, oestrogen acts on oestrogen receptors in bone, brain and vagina and also makes the womb lining grow, and a progestin acting on progesterone receptors protects the lining. Oestrogen given alone raises the risk of womb lining overgrowth, so women with a womb are given a progestin as well.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.

nodes.label: Androgen signal
nodes.info: Testosterone and its active form dihydrotestosterone acting on the androgen receptor.

nodes.label: Oestrogen signal
nodes.info: Oestradiol acting on the oestrogen receptor in bone, brain, vagina and womb.

nodes.label: Oestrogen drive
nodes.info: Oestrogen makes the womb lining thicken.

nodes.label: Progestin protection
nodes.info: Progestin turns the lining from growth to shedding.

nodes.label: Androgen effect
nodes.info: A teaching score for androgen action (muscle, libido, body hair, voice).

nodes.label: Oestrogen effect
nodes.info: A teaching score for oestrogen action on bone, vessels and menopausal symptoms (hot flushes, vaginal dryness).

nodes.label: Womb lining risk
nodes.info: A teaching score for overgrowth of the womb lining. Oestrogen alone makes the lining grow and raises the risk of hyperplasia and cancer; a progestin balances it.

edges.label: androgen receptor
edges.info: Testosterone replacement and androgenic drugs such as danazol act on the androgen receptor. High levels cause acne, hair growth, polycythaemia and, in women, virilisation.
More androgen action raises the androgen effect.

edges.label: oestrogen receptor
edges.info: Menopausal hormone therapy gives oestrogen for hot flushes, vaginal dryness and bone protection. Tibolone has oestrogen, progestin and androgen effects.
More oestrogen action raises the oestrogen effect.

edges.label: lining growth
edges.info: Oestrogen makes the lining grow. A progestin (or a progestin-releasing device) counters this, which is why women with a womb are given oestrogen with a progestin.
More growth raises the lining risk.

edges.label: progesterone receptor
edges.info: Progesterone and progestins act on the lining to stop growth and make it shed.
More progestin lowers the lining risk.

sources: Where each class acts. Testosterone acts on androgen receptors, oestrogen on oestrogen receptors (and makes the womb lining grow), and progestin protects the womb lining. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Transdermal versus oral routes, thrombosis and breast cancer risk, timing of menopause therapy, vaginal oestrogen, selective modulators (own figure), cyproterone and anti-androgens (own figure), puberty induction, gender-affirming care, doping, contraindications and monitoring are left out. The three results are teaching scores. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
